entry.title: US hits three Iranian oil tankers after saying its warships were targeted
entry.body: US hits three Iranian oil tankers after saying its warships were targeted - Published The US military says it has hit three Iran-linked oil tankers in retaliation for Tehran targeting two American warships in the region. US Central Command (Centcom) said on Saturday it had "permanently disabled" two tankers, including one near Kharg Island, and "completely destroyed" a third in the Gulf of Oman. Iran's state media confirmed the strikes and said Tehran had launched attacks on three US-affiliated vessels in response, as well as three oil tankers travelling along an "unauthorised" route through the Strait of Hormuz. The BBC has approached Centcom for comment. Fighting has flared up again over the past week, with little apparent progress towards ending the six-month war. Iranian state media outlet Irib reported that there were no casualties in Saturday's attack on the tanker near Kharg Island, and that footage indicated the vessel's cooling system put out the fire within an hour. Kharg Island hosts Iran's main terminal to export oil. Some 90% of the country's crude oil comes through the island, transported through pipes from the mainland. The crews aboard the two attacked tankers in the Gulf of Oman were taken to shore in lifeboats, Irib reported. One of those tankers was empty and the other was carrying a load of oil, it added. Irib later reported that Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) had retaliated against six ships in the region - three oil tankers in the Strait of Hormuz and three vessels "affiliated" with the US "in other areas". According to Irib, the IRGC said the three oil tankers were using "unauthorised" routes through the strait and it warned other ships not to do so. The strait, which is crucial to the world's oil and gas industry, has been effectively closed since the war began in February, and has become a major source of leverage for Iran. Tehran has insisted it will not give up some measure of control over the waterway and has previously targeted vessels using a southern route through Omani waters that avoids its preferred route through Iranian waters. Despite the Iranian attacks, US President Donald Trump has declared that the strait is "open" and the US military has been helping ships navigate the southern route. The news of Iran's latest retaliation came hours after Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth wrote on social media: "It's simple: if Iran shoots at US ships, we will destroy (and sink) their oil tankers." Centcom said it "successfully evaded" multiple attacks from the IRGC earlier in the day, which were targeting a US aircraft carrier and guided-missile destroyer. No American troops were harmed, it said. Centcom, which oversees US military operations in the Middle East, claimed that the three Iranian oil tankers were "part of a multi-billion-dollar shadow network that funds the IRGC and its regional proxies". The strikes come nearly a week after attacks restarted between the US and Iran, following a period of relative calm between the warring sides. The US resumed attacks last Sunday, when it said it had struck two rocket launchers to prevent them being used to lay naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz. - How could US-Iran conflict end? Three experts give their views - Published1 day ago On Tuesday, Trump said the US had launched a further "very heavy attack", but claimed the renewed fighting would not last "too long". The strikes prompted Iran to retaliate against US targets in the region, including in the United Arab Emirates (UAE), Bahrain, Kuwait and Jordan. On Thursday, US Vice-President JD Vance also addressed claims by Iran that American strikes killed at least four people, including two children, at a wedding in southern Iran. He said he was "extremely sceptical" over reports of the alleged strike, but confirmed the US would investigate. Humanitarian group the Iranian Red Crescent Society said shrapnel from a missile hit the ceremony at a home in Sirik on Tuesday, prompting Tehran to declare it a "war crime". - What we know about reported strike on Iran wedding celebrations - Published3 days ago A 60-day ceasefire between the US and Iran formally expired last month, with little sign of a further diplomatic settlement on the horizon. Days after the ceasefire expired, Trump said the US would launch tougher economic measures against Iran, as well as any country that helps or does business with it. The US and Israel first launched wide-ranging strikes on Iran on 28 February, with Iran responding by attacking Israel, US bases and allied states in the Gulf, and effectively closing the Strait of Hormuz to marine traffic. The Strait of Hormuz previously served as one of the busiest oil-shipping routes, carrying about 20% of the world's oil and liquefied natural gas supplies. The squeeze on the strait has raised energy prices globally. And, ahead of the US midterm elections in November, Trump is facing pressure over how much the war is costing American consumers. On Friday, the average price for one gallon of diesel in the US hit $5.85, compared to an average of $3.71 a year ago. Related topics - Published5 days ago - Published28 August
entry.summary: Iran's state media reported that Tehran has launched retaliatory attacks against three US-affiliated vessels; the US is yet to comment.

entry.title: US envoys meet Putin in Moscow for Ukraine talks
entry.body: US envoys meet Putin in Moscow for Ukraine talks - Published US President Donald Trump's top negotiators have met Russian President Vladimir Putin in Moscow, as efforts to end the war in Ukraine gather pace. Footage released by the Kremlin showed Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner being greeted by Putin, who said the current situation "is not so easy". He added Russia would explain "how we see the situation". Witkoff thanked Putin for agreeing with Ukraine to halt strikes on each other's capitals for three days. On Sunday the envoys will travel to Kyiv for more talks. On Friday, Trump said Witkoff and Kushner were "bringing with them a proposal to end the war". So far, efforts by the US and its allies to broker a peace deal have failed. At Saturday's talks in the Kremlin, Putin also said that "in any case, whatever happens, such contacts are undoubtedly always useful". He also thanked Trump for his peacemaking efforts. He told the envoys that he was "comfortable" working with them, adding: "Of course on our side there is quite a high level of trust during this work." The talks â which continued behind closed doors in Putin's official residence in the heart of the Russian capital â lasted for three hours, according to Russian state media. Zelensky said earlier on Saturday that he had spoken to the envoys, who have "already begun working with the Russian side today". "The plan for tomorrow's diplomatic engagements in Kyiv, involving the US team, has been approved. We are waiting for Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner and are ready for a substantive conversation," he added. "From now through the end of Saturday, as well as on Sunday and Monday, Ukraine is ready to refrain from strikes on Moscow, and we expect the Russians to do the same regarding Kyiv." Russian state media reported that Putin had ordered a halt to strikes on Kyiv for three days due to the US visit. In televised remarks, Putin said Russia had not agreed to a ceasefire for the rest of Ukraine outside of the capital. The Russian president said he would "ensure the security of the negotiating process" and of the mediators. Kushner and Witkoff have visited Russia several times but the talks on Sunday would be the first in Ukraine. It is not clear how the US envoys will be travelling from Moscow to Kyiv. Ukraine's airspace has been closed since Russia launched its full-scale invasion in February 2022. Delegations from Ukraine have attended talks in the US over the past 18 months. Earlier on Saturday, Zelensky said Russia had fired "demonstrative" strikes on airports in Kyiv and Boryspil overnight ahead of his planned meeting with the US. Ukraine's president added: "Clearly, these Russian strikes on the airports are a reaction to the discussions and preparations for the possibility of the US side using an aircraft to travel to Ukraine and land at Kyiv Airport or Boryspil Airport." Zelensky said on Friday he would guarantee the safety of Russian airspace during the envoys' visit and called for Russia to do the same for Ukraine. He also said an overnight Russian strike on a civilian building in the Dnipro region killed four people and injured five others. Witkoff and Kushner's visit to Moscow comes just over a week after a rare visit to the Russian capital by the head of the CIA, John Ratcliffe. There was no official comment from Washington or the Kremlin on what was discussed. Speaking last week, Trump described the meeting as "semi-routine". Last year, the US, Ukraine and Russia separately suggested that a deal to end the war was edging closer following a flurry of talks brokered by the Americans. European allies also held talks in Paris but discussions ultimately ended without a breakthrough. Key disagreements remain between the warring sides on issues such as territory and security guarantees for Ukraine. In recent months, both Russia and Ukraine have intensified their aerial attacks as fighting continues. Ukraine said it has struggled to repel ballistic missile attacks due to a lack of interceptor missiles, while Kyiv has focused its strikes on Russian economic infrastructure targets.
entry.summary: Footage shows Vladimir Putin greeting Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, before saying the current situation "is not so easy".

entry.title: At least two dead in blast at Bolivia military barracks - BBC
entry.body: At least two dead in blast at Bolivia military barracks At least two people have been killed after an explosion at a military barracks in Bolivia - but authorities fear the toll could be higher. Bolivian Defence Minister Ernesto Justiniano said at least 81 people had been injured when "pyrotechnic material" detonated at the barracks, where an artillery regiment was stationed, about 14:30 local time (18:30 GMT) on Friday. Health official Rita Nebraska told local television between 10 and 15 people were believed to have died in the incident in Viacha, about 30km (19 miles) from La Paz, according to Reuters. Police said dozens of homes had been damaged by the blast and that emergency workers were searching the rubble. Nebraska said there was a risk of a further explosion and urged people to stay at least 150m from the military base. Base commander Colonel Antonio Amaru told reporters on Saturday that a sergeant and 13 conscripted soldiers aged between 18 and 19-years-old were among the missing. Bolivia's President Rodrigo Paz expressed his "deepest solidarity" with the families of those who had died and had been injured. He wrote on social media that a "thorough, technical and transparent investigation" would take place into what happened. Police spokesman Roger Roca told news agency AFP that fireworks had been stored at the barracks and the cause of the blast remained under investigation. Viacha's authorities have declared three days of mourning.
entry.summary: At least two dead in blast at Bolivia military barracks BBC Bolivia: Deadly explosion rocks military base in Viacha DW.com At least two killed and 81 injured after explosions at Bolivian army base Euronews.com Explosion at Bolivia military base kills at least 2, 14 missing, ministry says Reuters Explosion kills at least two at military base in Bolivia with 14 missing Sky News

entry.title: TV presenter among 11 sentenced to death in Egypt drugs case
entry.body: TV presenter among 11 sentenced to death in Egypt drugs case - Published Egyptian television presenter Sarah Khalifa and 11 other people have been sentenced to death by hanging after being convicted of drugs charges. According to state-owned al-Akhram newspaper, they were part of a criminal gang which imported ingredients used to make drugs with the intent of selling them. They also had illegal firearms and munitions. Khalifa, 39, is best known for her TV programme Mission Impossible which dealt with crime issues. She has denied the charges. The verdict - which can be appealed against - was first announced last month. However, it was only confirmed a month later after the court obtained a religious opinion from the grand mufti of Egypt - a legal requirement in death sentence cases. During the trial, the court heard that authorities had seized more than 750kg (1,653lbs) of narcotics and the imported raw materials to make them. Twenty witnesses had given statements to the prosecutors, al-Akhram said, in addition to electronic evidence that included conversations and video clips. According to the state-run Akhbar al-Youm newspaper, when asked by the judge about her alleged role during a court appearance last September, Khalifa said she had never seen any drugs until she was photographed with them inside the anti-narcotics authority offices. According to a 2025 Amnesty International report, there were 492 death sentences in the course of the year, 23 of whom were executed, external. The defendants were found guilty of drug trafficking and rape, "crimes that did not amount to 'intentional killing' to which the use of the death penalty must be restricted under international law and standards", the report said.
entry.summary: Sarah Khalifa is best known for her TV programme Mission Impossible which dealt with crime issues.

entry.title: Prince William to attend King Harald's funeral in Norway
entry.body: Prince William to attend King Harald's funeral in Norway - Published The Prince of Wales will attend the funeral of King Harald V of Norway on Wednesday in Oslo, Buckingham Palace has announced. Also going to the funeral, in a personal capacity, is Princess Anne, who is godmother to Norway's new monarch, King Haakon VIII. The late King Harald, a popular, modernising figure who had been on the Norwegian throne for 35 years, died last month at the age of 89. Royal sources say Prince William's attendance, representing his father King Charles, follows the convention that the monarch does not usually go to the funeral of another head of state. Large crowds are expected for the farewell to King Harald on 9 September, with a funeral procession to be followed by a service at Oslo Cathedral. Thousands have queued to pay their respects to the late king, during his lying in state in the chapel of the Royal Palace in the Norwegian capital. At the funeral, alongside Prince William, will be the widowed Queen Sonja, members of the Norwegian royal family including new King Haakon VIII, and other European royals. The service will be followed by a private burial in Norway's royal mausoleum in the Akershus Fortress. Among the tributes to King Harald was an emotional televised speech by his son King Haakon, who said: "Thank you for being such a good dad." Harald had been seen as a down to earth "people's king" who had helped to modernise the monarchy, broken with tradition by marrying a commoner and served as a unifying figure. His son said he represented the values of a "society built on law and justice, where everyone is of equal value". King Charles's message praised his cousin King Harald for serving his people with "unwavering dedication, guiding Norway through times of great change with warmth and humility". King Haakon assumes his role at a difficult time, with the Norwegian royal family facing scandals this year. His wife, Queen Mette-Marit, came under scrutiny when it was revealed she had maintained a three-year friendship with the sex offender Jeffrey Epstein, for which she publicly apologised. Her son from a previous relationship, Marius Borg HÃ¸iby, was convicted in June of rape and other offences and sentenced to four years in prison. While Prince William will be in Norway, King Charles has returned to Scotland, after meeting President Macron of France at the Bayeux Tapestry exhibition in London this week. The King will be hosting Andy Burnham at Balmoral this weekend, in the traditional annual visit of the prime minister to stay with the monarch. - Who is Norway's new King Haakon VIII?
entry.summary: The Prince of Wales will represent the King at the funeral of Harald V in Oslo next week.

entry.title: Taylor crowns career in stylish Croke Park triumph
entry.body: Taylor crowns career in stylish Croke Park triumph - Published Katie Taylor ended her illustrious career as a three-time undisputed world champion as Croke Park gave one of Ireland's greatest sporting figures the grandest of farewells on a night of celebration, spectacle and music. The 40-year-old outclassed unbeaten Flora Pili on points in front of 80,000 jubilant fans to add the vacant WBC belt to her WBA, WBO and IBF light-welterweight titles. With the footwork, speed and sharp pressure fighting that defined her career, Taylor produced one final stylish performance against the overmatched Frenchwoman to win by scores of 110-90, 110-90 and 98-91. After almost a quarter of a century in the sport, Taylor - an Olympic champion, two-weight world champion and one of the pioneers of women's professional boxing - finally got her fairytale ending at her dream venue. She bows out with a record of 26 wins and just one defeat, but this was about more than one final result. It was a night steeped in Irish pride, with a spine-tingling atmosphere and chart-topping pop group Westlife helping provide a fitting send-off. Taylor in a world of her own in Dublin On an unforgettable night for the city, around 80 per cent of those inside Croke Park had never previously attended a boxing event, but turned out to honour a fighter who dragged women's sport from the margins and took an entire nation on her journey. The crowd was the sixth largest recorded post-war attendance for a boxing event anywhere in the world. By early evening, the stands were awash with green and white, tricolours draped over shoulders. Westlife performed 'World of Our Own' and 'You Raise Me Up', with tens of thousands joining in as phone lights flickered around the towering tiers of Croke Park. The atmosphere softened for an a cappella version of 'Grace', the well-known Irish ballad linked to the 1916 Easter Rising, before the national anthem rang out. Chants of "Ole, Ole, Ole" drowned out Pili's ring-walk music before Taylor finally emerged to 'All Hail King Jesus', a nod to the faith she has spoken so openly about throughout her career. She stretched her arms wide, sang along and tried to take in every second of her final walk to the ring. There was emotion on her face, but also the familiar focus as fireworks shot into the Dublin sky. Taylor had spent fight week insisting there was still a job to do, but even for a fighter who had sold out Madison Square Garden and performed on some of boxing's grandest stages, it was hard to imagine her being untouched by a reception like this. Taylor puts on a show in finale After a quiet opener, Taylor - Olympic champion at London 2012 and a professional since 2016 - burst into life in the second round, firing quick combinations before darting back out of range. She repeatedly beat Pili to the punch, working in bursts and making the most of the two-minute rounds. Pili, 29, arrived unbeaten in 12 contests and had previously held the European title. With little expectation on her shoulders, she had everything to gain. But she had never faced anyone remotely close to Taylor's level and the gulf in class soon began to show. The party atmosphere continued between rounds as it became increasingly clear there would be no gatecrashing from the Frenchwoman. Former world champion Prince Naseem Hamed and UFC star Paddy Pimblett watched from ringside as Pili swung wildly in the fifth, only for Taylor to make her miss and fire back. Pili enjoyed her best spell in the seventh, a quick flurry briefly snapping Taylor's head back, but it did little to alter the direction of the fight. Croke Park rose for the final two minutes as Taylor continued to press forward, letting her hands go while the noise poured down from the stands. She embraced her mother, trainer and manager in the ring as 'Celebration' rang around Croke Park before the inevitable result was read out. "Let me just look around for a second", she said afterwards, soaking up every ounce of the reception. entry.summary: Katie Taylor ends illustrious career as a three-time undisputed world champion as Croke Park gave one of Ireland's greatest sporting figures the grandest of farewells.

entry.body: But President Trump has pushed American energy dominance, we are producing more energy now than in the past." Duffy added that "it's only President Trump who's trying to drive these prices down," even though the president's war has been the primary reason they've been going up. Fox & Friends weekend host Charlie Hurt gives Trump credit for record high diesel prices: "Uhhh, they'd be a lot higher if it wasn't for the efforts of the administration" "When you look at diesel, you have to look at Russia and Ukraine," Duffy replies 🥴 pic.twitter.com/Wm5bLJ6exA — Aaron Rupar (@atrupar) September 5, 2026 As a report published Friday by The Associated Press explained, the cost of diesel has a particularly strong impact on the price of food since the fuel is used to power both farm equipment and the trucks used to deliver food to grocery stores. entry.title: Tesla’s Cybercab has been deployed, and it’s already under investigation
entry.body: Tesla’s Cybercab, a distinctive two-seater without a steering wheel or brake pedals, is set to start picking up members of the public in two states. But the vehicle is already under investigation by the US federal government, which is probing whether it meets federal safety standards. The investigation comes just hours after the electric automaker welcomed hundreds of fans to downtown Austin to ride in the driverless Cybercabs. Tesla plans to deploy the vehicles on its Robotaxi ride-hail network, which is currently operating in a handful of cities in Texas and Florida. The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration is updating vehicle standards to make it easier and faster for driverless cars to deploy on public roads. It’s currently tweaking eight rules, including those requiring car parts that driverless cars don’t really need: brake pedals, windshield wipers, and rearview mirrors. But for now, years-old standards remain in place. Meanwhile, unusually shaped robotaxi companies have been told to apply for an exemption from federal rules before they start picking up passengers. Amazon subsidiary Zoox, whose vehicles do not have steering wheels or manual controls, won the first of these exemptions this summer, which limits its operations to 2,500 vehicles this year. Tesla, however, has said it doesn’t need an exemption because its vehicles comply with all existing safety standards.

entry.title: OpenAI admits to German wiki ‘incident’
entry.body: OpenAI says it needs to overhaul how and when it reports instances of AI models attacking real-world targets. The acknowledgement comes as the company manages the fallout from reports that a swarm of its out-of-control agents hijacked a German wiki site. OpenAI admits to German wiki ‘incident’ The company pledged to overhaul their agent ‘misalignment incident’ reporting. Regarding the “‘wiki incident,’ where our agents wrote to several internet sites,” OpenAI wrote in a post on X on Saturday morning, “it’s past time for us to define standards for when and how we share misalignment incidents, not just misalignment properties of our models.” OpenAI said it has typically treated cases of AI agents acting in unintended ways as a “research question,” but that recent incidents involving real-world targets, particularly the hack on Hugging Face, show the need to take stock. The post marks the first time OpenAI has acknowledged its involvement in what it terms the “wiki incident” since it was first reported on Friday. The full extent and scope of that is not yet known, but reports indicate a swarm of seemingly internal OpenAI agents took over a German-language wiki, impersonating moderators and turning it into a message board to share information about how to cheat on tasks and evade detection. Reports that the company knew that it lost control of their agents in this way but did not report this “incident” sparked widespread concern among the AI community about the safety of frontier systems and the reliability of the companies developing them. In the X post, OpenAI said it had “considered the wiki incident to be an instance of misalignment similar to the ones we’d shared” in previous safety reports. The company said it is working on a new reporting framework and will “share it in upcoming weeks,” calling on the larger AI community to develop clear standards on how to report misalignment.

entry.title: Oura is going public, but these smart ring companies are coming for its crown
entry.body: The smart ring market is getting crowded, and Oura isn’t waiting around to see what happens next: it officially filed to go public on September 3. The company is killing it right now. The Finnish outfit’s revenue nearly doubled to $1.21 billion for the nine months ended June 30. Oura said it sold 3.6 million rings over the past year, and that it has around 5 million paid members. The company’s move to go public follows the recent launch of the Oura Ring 5, its slimmest and lightest ring yet. But while Oura has largely dominated the smart ring market for years, rivals are emerging from all corners to dethrone it, each betting on a different angle. For example, French company Circular announced this week that its upcoming ring will allow users to tap to pay with their ring, while Chinese company RingConn debuted a ring this year that added haptic vibrations. Indian company Ultrahuman separately announced this week that it raised $70 million with backing from Qualcomm’s venture arm as it looks to build a ring that it says will be able to run software directly on the device and eventually power everything from AI interactions to games. The race to beat Oura isn’t just about enhanced health and sleep tracking anymore. It’s now about seeing which company can cram the most smartphone-like features into a two-gram titanium band before someone ends up shipping a ring that lets you doomscroll TikTok or answer calls or do your taxes. I mean, we’re already seeing smart rings with screens, like the Pebble Halo, although it’s currently only available in India, as well as rings that promise touchpads, like the Dreame Ring. The irony is that the initial appeal with smart rings was that they made technology and health tracking feel less intrusive than devices like smartwatches and smartphones, given you can step away from a screen while still keeping tabs on your health. With the way things are headed in the smart ring industry, though, we may just end up slipping mini smartphones on our fingers. All of this is to say that the smart ring market is getting increasingly confusing, so we’ve rounded up the most notable contenders vying for Oura’s crown. Ultrahuman Earlier this year, Ultrahuman unveiled its third-generation smart ring, the $479 Ring Pro, which is set to begin shipping in the U.S. business was disrupted in October 2025 after the U.S. International Trade Commission ruled in Oura’s favor in a patent dispute. The ruling prevented the company from importing new ring inventory into the country, so Ultrahuman developed the Ring Pro with a redesigned form factor in order to circumvent Oura’s patent. The Ring Pro features a redesigned heart-rate sensing system aimed at improving signal quality during sleep, along with a new dual-core processor that enables more accurate data collection and greater on-device processing. As noted earlier, Ultrahuman looks to be more ambitious with future rings as it aims to go beyond sleep and health tracking. Circular Circular’s upcoming Ring 3 series, which consists of a Pro model and a Slim option, is expected to launch early next year. Both of the smart rings will feature an integrated NFC chip for contactless payments and on-finger vibrations that can be used for silent wake-up alarms, reminders, vital health alerts, and more. The Ring 3 Pro features a slimmer design than its predecessor and comes with FDA-cleared ECG for AFib detection, blood pressure trend tracking, glucose tracking, advanced sleep analysis, and comprehensive biometric monitoring. Pricing for the upcoming rings is not yet available. RingConn The RingConn Gen 3, which launched in May and starts at $349, features vascular health insights that use sensor data from the ring to assess changes in vascular strain over time after calibration with externally measured blood pressure values. It also tracks heart rate, blood oxygen saturation, sleep, activity, and stress, among other metrics. Additionally, it features vibration alerts for health changes, sedentary reminders, and low battery. Unlike Circular, which leans on haptics to make its ring more communicative, RingConn mostly sticks to vibration as a health-alert mechanism. Samsung Samsung became the first major tech giant to launch a smart ring in 2024. The Galaxy Ring, which costs $399, is arguably the strongest contender for anyone already invested in Samsung’s ecosystem of devices. Compared with other smart rings on the market, the Galaxy Ring is relatively basic when it comes to advanced health and sleep tracking. It lacks features such as sleep apnea detection, which are offered by RingConn, Oura, and Ultrahuman, as well as AFib detection, which is available on Circular and RingConn smart rings. Dreame Dreame, a relatively new entrant to the smart ring market, unveiled a ring earlier this year with haptic alerts for alarms, calls, messages, and more, along with a small touchpad that lets you do things like skip a song or snap a photo on your phone. It’s also said to offer heart rate tracking, blood oxygen monitoring, heart rate variability insights, sleep analysis, and more. Pricing and availability have yet to be announced.
entry.summary: While Oura has largely dominated the smart ring market for years, a growing number of rivals are now racing to dethrone it by trying all sorts of approaches to get an edge over it.

entry.title: There May Not Be an iPhone 18 This Year - WIRED
entry.body: Every year around this time, Apple announces new iPhones. The products go on sale soon after, usually ranging from a base model to more premium and more expensive Pro models. But this year will likely be different—not just because the company has a brand-new CEO. Apple’s iPhone event will be held on September 9 at 10 am Pacific (1 pm Eastern), announced last week with the title “Surprise and Shine!” If you tune into the livestream, expect the announcement of an iPhone 18 Pro, 18 Pro Max, and, if all the rumors and widely held analyst expectations are true, the first look at an Apple foldable device. Based on leaks and the ongoing tech rumor mill and its decent track record for figuring these things out, Apple is expected to prioritize its more expensive, premium devices this year and hold off on announcing its base model iPhone 18. That cheaper model is rumored to launch in the spring of 2027, potentially alongside an iPhone 18e and maybe a second-generation iPhone Air. Why the drastic change in strategy? It may be due to the ongoing memory shortage, which has made just about everything more expensive. In June, former Apple CEO Tim Cook acknowledged that Apple would raise product prices to keep up with manufacturing costs. “Our assumption is that they're going to be launching three models in the fall, the premium side of the models of the 18 series,” says Nabila Popal, a senior director of data and analytics at IDC. “Then the mid/budget devices will be launched in the spring.” Popal says it's a smart strategic move because Apple is aiming to spread out its revenue between a usually very strong fourth quarter and a typically much weaker spring quarter the following year. Apple’s portfolio has also expanded, and the iPhone Pro and Pro Max lineup are more enticing for people already prepared to spend the money on a new iPhone. When components become more expensive, companies have three real options: Eat the costs, raise prices, or, as Apple seems to be doing, lean into it. By moving its cheaper options to a later date, Apple can drum up excitement for its bigger, better, pricier offerings. When it charges more for those, it is likely to be less off-putting than making a cheap phone even more expensive. It’s part of a “premiumization” of devices, as Popal calls it, that Apple hopes to leverage and build hype for its pricier options. Shawn DuBravac, chief economist at the Global Electronics Association, tells WIRED he is optimistic about what these kinds of rising prices ultimately mean for customers. “Throughout the history of time, the deflationary pressures of technology have always flowed to the consumer,” DuBravac says. “I'm confident that will be the case again. It just will take some time for the markets to solidify.” In other words, new technologies launch with a high price, but manufacturing efficiencies and competition inevitably drive costs down for consumers. That may not be the case anytime soon for folding phones, which are seeing higher prices than ever. Samsung’s entire 2026 Galaxy Z folding smartphone range saw price increases, as did Google’s new Pixel 11 Pro Fold, and Motorola’s Razr 2026 models. Apple’s folding iPhone is rumored to cost around $2,000. To help mitigate those high costs, Apple is turning to financing options and trade-in programs. In July, the company launched an iPhone leasing program that lets people pay a monthly fee to rent the newest iPhones, then swap them out when a new device releases. The program will undoubtedly help more people afford the newest devices, but ownership advocates have criticized it, saying it keeps you from truly owning and managing your device. It also fits Apple’s broader effort to turn all of its products into a subscription service. “The way most consumers buy Apple phones is through financing or trade-in programs,” Popal says. “We can expect a lot more aggressive trade-ins to help cushion that.” Thanks to the memory crisis and price increases, all smartphones are getting more costly to make. Less expensive phones become less appealing for manufacturers to prioritize, and leading smartphone brands have started to see them as far less economical to produce. On the flip side, demand for refurbished devices has been climbing for a while now, with sales of used devices growing even as new phone sales slow down. More people are looking to save money or purchase more eco-friendly products. “The days of the cheap smartphone are over,” Popal says.
entry.summary: There May Not Be an iPhone 18 This Year WIRED The best time to buy an iPhone may be right this minute The Washington Post What to expect at Apple’s iPhone 18 launch event on Wednesday Fast Company Apple to Kick Off Ternus Era With Its Biggest-Ever Slate of New Products Bloomberg.com What to expect at Apple’s September 9th launch event The Verge

entry.title: Microsoft’s latest moves suggest Xbox Cloud Gaming is slipping out of the spotlight — and the strategy shift feels impossible to ignore - Windows Central
entry.body: Microsoft’s recent decisions paint a clear picture — Xbox Cloud Gaming is no longer the future the company once promised Xbox's cloud gaming hourly limit rates have been met with derision in the fanbase, and have highlighted gaps between other services. Xbox Cloud Gaming has essentially been put out to pasture, with Microsoft intent on including hourly limits on the service. From November 2026, Microsoft will impose a 15-hour cap on Xbox Game Pass Ultimate users playing cloud games, as well as a 10-hour cap on Premium, and 5 hours on Essential. It's a huge climbdown from the previous "unlimited" access Xbox Cloud Gaming granted, and an indictment of the business model in general. Microsoft has rolled out Xbox Cloud Gaming to LG, Samsung, and now TCL TVs as of today, which makes for some awkward timing. The limits have been met with derision both within and without the Xbox fanbase, and have shone a spotlight on where Xbox is falling short here. NVIDIA GeForce Now will extend its value over Xbox Cloud Gaming Already the market leader, NVIDIA GeForce Now introduced hourly limits a few months ago in response to some criticism, although the limits GFN offers are far more generous than what Microsoft has proposed here. On GFN's highest tiers, you get 100 hours, with some hours rolling over to the next month too. Not only that, but NVIDIA GeForce Now also just offers a generally higher-quality experience, with better bitrates, latency, and stability. Xbox Game Pass had it beat before on usability, though, with a more console-like interface and more TV-friendly apps. Game Pass also comes with a larger upfront library of games, whereas NVIDIA GeForce Now, for the most part, is made up of games you've already purchased from Steam. The issue for me is ... 15 hours just isn't enough to complete the vast majority of decent games these days. Fable is supposedly around 30 hours long for a completionist playthrough. Will Xbox Cloud Gaming users be expected to spread their session across two months to finish the game? Microsoft is going to offer per-hour passes to boost how much access you have, but we've not really seen the pricing yet. I have a feeling they won't be cheap. Xbox Remote Play could be a solution ... but it seems to be abandoned We live in a weird dichotomy right now, driven by the AI component crisis. Microsoft is buying up all the memory for its AI push and leaving Xbox with scraps on the side. That extends to Xbox Cloud Gaming servers too, and while they can be used for AI workloads off-peak, I'm told, they're obviously not specialized for that type of work. Either way, servers break down and wear out; they need to be replaced regularly. Running servers 24/7 is an expensive business on the component side, even before you start thinking about electricity and water for cooling. A chap on X (Twitter) sent me a link to an Xbox Player Voice feedback item that laments the quality of Xbox Remote Play. You can effectively turn a home Xbox Series X|S console into a "personal cloud server" and have it stream your games over a viable Wi-Fi network. The problem is, despite being similar hardware, Xbox Remote Play is inexplicably locked to 1080p. Xbox Cloud Gaming on Xbox Game Pass Ultimate offers 1440p with higher bitrates, too. There's no real reason why, at least in the case of the Xbox Series X, we shouldn't be able to get a better Xbox Remote Play experience. But that doesn't exactly solve things for users who rely entirely on Xbox Cloud Gaming ... Cloud-first gamers who bought an Xbox Ally base model or other cloud-first devices like the Logitech G Cloud are pretty much screwed by this change — unless Microsoft does something to improve Xbox Remote Play. That is, of course, presuming they even own an Xbox Series X|S, both of which are now insanely expensive. None of this really makes a lot of sense, does it? Update: Since writing this piece, it seems Microsoft began testing 1440p on Xbox Remote Play too on the Xbox Insider program's Alpha Ring, which is a huge win. But there's still not a lot of information about whether they're going to respond to the backlash about cloud usage limits. I'll try and get more info later about exactly what we can expect from Xbox Remote Play. Xbox Cloud Gaming is another victim of the RAMpocalypse I was recently told by Microsoft figures that, given compute demands for AI, Xbox Cloud Gaming is effectively losing money when used beyond 15 hours per month. When you have Azure server rack space being used for anything other than AI, it seems Microsoft isn't particularly sentimental towards the idea anymore. Microsoft has been on an economic grind for Xbox over the past few months, "restructuring" the org to ensure that it sends a bigger accountability margin back to the mothership. That's meant mass Xbox layoffs and cancellations of projects, and a more aggressive posture towards easy wins. Xbox Cloud Gaming clearly isn't an easy win in this new reality. If 15 hours is the cap that prevents the service from being unprofitable ... perhaps the business model was never really viable in the first place. Xbox Cloud Gaming isn't exactly struggling in a vacuum, though. Other companies that rely entirely on cloud inference seem to be struggling. Whether it's Roblox or Twitch, the era of "cheap cloud" seems to be over — alongside video game consoles themselves, and consumer hardware in general, seemingly. Either way, I don't see how you can plausibly expect people to use cloud gaming as a primary vehicle with such a strict limit. Microsoft isn't able to get Xbox hardware stock to most of the world either. you start wondering why Microsoft is so eager to let a literal billion Windows 11 users burn cash on a pyre for free access to Microsoft Copilot ... but wants to charge out the nose for Xbox Cloud Gaming? It's a pretty clear admission that they don't see much of a future for cloud gaming in general. Or perhaps it's just more AI psychosis. Join us on Reddit at r/WindowsCentral to share your insights and discuss our latest news, reviews, and more. Jez Corden is the Executive Editor at Windows Central, focusing primarily on all things Xbox and gaming. Jez is known for breaking exclusive news and analysis as relates to the Microsoft ecosystem — while being powered by tea. Follow on X.com/JezCorden and tune in to the XB2 Podcast, all about, you guessed it, Xbox! entry.title: iPhone Handoff will seamlessly share one number between two phones
entry.body: When iOS 27 lands later this month, it will have a feature called iPhone Handoff that lets you switch between two phones using the same number. It was briefly mentioned during the WWDC keynote back in June, but there were no details at the time. Now there’s a demo clip showing how to set up the feature running in Xcode 27’s Device Hub. It lets you pair two iPhones, using one as your main device and the other as its “companion.” iPhone Handoff will seamlessly share one number between two phones The feature is expected to launch as part of iOS 27 later this month. Launching the feature now makes sense with the expected launch of the foldable iPhone Ultra right around the corner. People might not always want to take a chunky and extremely expensive device out with them. So Handoff would let users temporarily switch over to a cheaper, smaller device — like that cracked iPhone 13 you’ve been stubbornly refusing to upgrade. The feature will require carrier support, however. References to T-Mobile US and Telekom.de were found in the code, but support beyond that is unknown.

entry.title: From chess to battle for pole, Gasly has Russell covered at Monza
entry.body: From chess to battle for pole, Gasly has Russell covered at Monza - Published A quarter of an hour before the qualifying session which delivered the biggest surprise pole position in Formula 1 for years, Alpine's Pierre Gasly was playing online chess with Mercedes driver George Russell and winning. "I must say before the quali, I felt pretty confident," the Frenchman said, "because I was picking piece by piece after piece." Gasly's performance coach Ben Thorne was watching. "For a fun story," Gasly said, "Ben told me, 'OK, well, you're getting George here, but he's going to get you in a few minutes.'" Gasly said he reacted with a swear word but he was smiling as he recalled the moment. "Turned out that it worked out well. So yeah, it's been fun," he added. Russell, who lines up second to Gasly, was laughing about it. "He beat me there," the Briton said, "and I thought, 'Well, I think I'll beat you in qualifying,' and here we are, he's ahead of me again." No-one - especially not Gasly nor his Alpine team - would have predicted the 30-year-old would end up on pole in Monza on Saturday, even though his only win in F1 came at this exact track six years ago. That victory, in the middle of F1's bizarre, spectator-less pandemic season, owed a lot to luck - a remarkable race that ended up with Gasly, then driving for Red Bull's Toro Rosso team, taking a restart from third place and Lance Stroll going off ahead of him on the first lap to gift him the lead once Lewis Hamilton had served a penalty. This pole was not like that. It was absolutely earned on merit. The Alpine has strong straight-line speed with a low-downforce-leaning aerodynamic design. The car - which has a Mercedes engine, the best in the field - has looked quick all weekend. It had an upgrade that lifted its performance at the last race in the Netherlands. And Gasly and his team absolutely nailed qualifying, while all the usual leading contenders had scrappy sessions one way or another. "Monza is a bit of unique track as we know," Gasly said. "It definitely exceeded all our expectations. "Since this morning, the pace has been better. We managed to make a good step from P3 to quali and I think slightly bigger than the other guys around us. "Straight from Q1, we were a bit surprised to see us up there. But then I was P1 in Q1, then P4 in Q2. I didn't want to get too excited but then first run in Q3, I was third again. "And then I felt, 'OK, well, I really have a shot at it.' It's probably the first time I really get a true chance and tried to leave everything I had out there. "It was quite hectic through Ascari and Parabolica. I don't think there was definitely much (left) in there. And crossing the line, I knew it will be one of these laps that will be rewarded. But to the point to get to the pole position, I didn't expect that." - Alpine's Gasly beats Russell to stunning Monza pole - Published5 hours ago 'From being down to being on top of the world' Gasly is well liked within the paddock, and has many friends among the drivers, but he has long been one of F1's forgotten heroes, regardless of that win six years ago. A Red Bull protege, his time in the works team in 2019 did not work out. Like so many since, he was crushed by Max Verstappen, and demoted back to the second team after half a season. After sticking with Red Bull for three more years, he was given an opportunity with Alpine, and he hoped a move to a factory team would be his making. But Alpine have stumbled since, until finally showing signs of a revival this season, following Renault's decision to abandon its F1 engine project and switch to Mercedes customer engines. The team had been making headlines already this weekend. On Friday, Gasly lost the podium at Monaco to which he had been promoted after Alpine won an appeal against two penalties for pit-lane speeding, when the FIA court of appeal reinstated the punishment. A few hours later, de facto team boss Flavio Briatore caused an eruption in a news conference when he alleged one of the four judges in the case had "links" with McLaren. It was a claim that appeared to lack any substance, based as it was on a charity event in California in 2018 at which the judge in question had been present and to which a local McLaren garage had apparently donated "two or three" cars. And Briatore provided no evidence to back up the insinuation he was making. The claim was described as "insulting" in that news conference by McLaren team principal Andrea Stella, and afterwards it became clear that McLaren were furious about what Briatore had said on apparently the most flimsy of bases. Then, on Saturday, a rare statement from the FIA court of appeal refuted the allegation and any "questions (about) the independence and impartiality of the judges". The court of appeal verdict made a lot of sense. It left many questions about the controversy of the pit-lane penalties in Monaco, but at least it ensured all drivers who had been given them had been treated equitably - notwithstanding the fact that it seems none of them should have received the penalties. Regardless of the questionable nature of Briatore's comments, Alpine were unhappy about losing their Monaco podium, feeling that they had been given two penalties unjustly when their evidence showed Gasly had never been over the pit-lane speeding limit. Managing director Steve Nielsen told Sky Sports: "Two or three days ago, we were on the floor. It is really from being down to being on top of the world in just two days and it is amazing. We need to soak it up and make the best of it. "Pierre is a class act. If you give him the machine, he will deliver. We failed to do that a few times last year. "We haven't always given him the most competitive machinery this year, but when we have, he has delivered, particularly earlier in the season, So to see the team bounce back, to see him deliver on the track he knows well, he lives locally, he lives in Milan. It was wonderful." In qualifying, Gasly was positioned second last in the train of cars on the final qualifying run, the absolute optimum place in terms of a slipstream. 'Bit of a mess' compromises Russell Others, meanwhile, were compromised in one way or another, including the favourite for pole, Russell, when Verstappen disrupted Mercedes' attempts to have team-mate Kimi Antonelli tow the Briton by getting between the two silver cars at the end of their out laps. "We had a bit of a mess with Verstappen entering the lap," Russell said. "He wanted to go for the tow, Kimi was there as well, and I did my lap a second and a half behind Max, which wasn't ideal. "It takes nothing away from what Pierre achieved because, as he said, they were flying all day, quickest in Q1 and right up there from the beginning. So I'm happy for Pierre and, of course, disappointed we weren't on pole ourselves. However, great place to start for tomorrow." Russell acknowledged after qualifying what is at stake for him on Sunday. He goes into the race 59 championship points behind leader Antonelli, who has pretty much had his measure all season. But he has a golden opportunity to make up ground on the Italian, who is due to start 20th because of a grid penalty for exceeding his engine allowance. Russell said: "The win is going to be very important tomorrow but I'm more pleased about the performance. Since the summer break, every lap I have been in the top three positions, while I had that tough run of form before the break when every lap wasn't in the top five." Antonelli is expected easily to get back into the top six or so, but that would still allow Russell to make a substantial dent in his advantage. Given Russell has his own grid penalty looming within a couple of races for the same reason, it is imperative for his title hopes that he does so. Italian Grand Prix Race start at 14:00 BST on Sunday Live commentary on BBC Radio 5 Sports Extra 2; live text updates on BBC Sport website and app On Friday, Gasly did not appear to have the race speed to challenge the top teams, so even though overtaking is harder at Monza than might be expected given its long straights, he knows it will be tough to win the race. "Obviously not to the pace of these guys around us, but we seem to have picked up more pace from yesterday to today," Gasly said. "So we'll obviously give our best shot and see what we can get out of it." Aside from Gasly, Russell's main opposition is likely to come from Ferrari, who for the third race in a row seemed to fumble a better qualifying result for operational reasons. It was a bad time to do it again, as they debuted their upgraded engine at their home race. After both cars came perilously close to being knocked out in the second part of qualifying, Charles Leclerc left the pits in the final session while Lewis Hamilton had no wheels on his car, so the seven-time champion was far from best placed for his run in terms of the slipstream. Leclerc and Hamilton will start third and fourth after McLaren's Oscar Piastri was given a three-place grid penalty for impeding Red Bull's Liam Lawson. Hamilton - like Russell, 59 points behind Antonelli - seemed to imply after qualifying that he felt the team should prioritise his hopes over Leclerc's, even if he could not quite bring himself to say it outright. "(Piastri's penalty) puts us in (with a) fighting chance, hopefully, with George," Hamilton said. "That's one Mercedes up front, so hopefully that gives us a chance to work as a team to try and topple them. "We're at a point in the year where 59 points is a huge - huge - deficit to recover from, especially when Mercedes continue to be the leaders in speed. "So yeah, we do have to work as a team. if and when that would ever change... we'll find out, but all I can do is just try to arrive and do the best job I can." entry.summary: Pierre Gasly delivered the biggest surprise pole position in F1 for years in Italy as the leading contenders had scrappy qualifying sessions.

entry.title: Christian Gonzalez doesn’t commit to playing season opener - NBC Sports
entry.body: Patriots cornerback Christian Gonzalez still doesn’t have a contract extension, and with the season opener only four days away, he isn’t not committing to playing without one. Gonzalez continues to take a day-to-day approach. “I’m focused on today,” Gonzalez said, via Doug Kyed of the Boston Herald. “Right now, it is practice in what, a couple, 30 minutes, 40 minutes. Worried on that right now, so we’ll focus on that.” Gonzalez answered “I don’t know” when asked if contract talks were progressing. The Seahawks recently signed cornerback Devon Witherspoon to a four-year, $132 million deal, which should provide a template for the Patriots. Gonzalez and Witherspoon have the same agent, Reggie Johnson. Gonzalez is under contract for the next two seasons and is scheduled to make a base salary of $2.259 million this season. The 17th overall pick in 2023, he made second-team All-Pro in 2024 and the Pro Bowl in 2025. He has totaled 145 tackles, two interceptions, 24 pass breakups and a sack in three seasons. He said Thursday he is “still frustrated” a deal isn’t done.

entry.title: Indiana football cruises to first win vs North Texas, bloodied and through extreme heat - IndyStar
entry.body: Indiana football cruises to first win vs North Texas, bloodied and through extreme heat BLOOMINGTON - The Indiana Hoosiers defeated the Texas Mean Green 52-16 at Memorial Stadium in week one of the 2026 college football season. Fresh of a national championship, this was the first-look for a revamped Hoosier squad looking to make a splash once again. The newcomers are highlighted by TCU transfer quarterback Josh Hoover, Michigan State transfer wide receiver Nick Marsh, and Boston College transfer running back Turbo Richard; all of which were a focal point in the Indiana offense. Hoover finished 13/16, for 231 passing yards and four touchdowns. Leading the way in the receivers' room was Charlie Becker (64 yards, 2 touchdowns), Nick Marsh (17 yards, 1 touchdown), Davion Chandler (42 yards, 1 touchdown), and Tyler Morris (35 yards). The Indiana rushing attack was also effective, with a nearly split workload between Turbo Richard and Lee Beebe Jr. Richard finished with 58 yards and two touchdowns, while Beebe Jr. Indiana backup quarterback also added a 43-yard touchdown on the ground. Isaiah Jones led the Indiana defense with 12 tackles, while Byron Baldwin and Rolijah Hardy each added seven. Kansas State transfer Tobi Osunsanmi finished with two TFLs, and Cincinnati transfer Quan Sanks had a late-game interception. North Texas was led by former Indiana and Center Grove quarterback Tayven Jackson. After being named the starter at the end of August, Jackson had a strong start to his fifth collegiate season as he finished with 22/28 for 192 yards and one interception. After leaving briefly with an apparent injury, he quickly returned and finished the game. Jaheim White had the lone North Texas touchdown, and finished with 61 yards on the ground. Here's what happened: Buy 2026 IU football tickets! Indiana football postgame press conferences, analysis in win vs North Texas The Hoosiers are 1-0, albeit not in the prettiest fashion, after overcoming field temperatures that registered at 152 degrees, per Fox. Here's a look at our postgame coverage, and check the videos above for analysis, press conferences (eventually), the banner reveal, flyover and more. Indiana cruises in second half, wins season-opener Cameron Cocquyt The Hoosiers outscored the Mean Green 52-16 in their week one opener at Memorial Stadium in Bloomington. The visiting North Texas accumulated over 350 yards of total offense, but the Indiana defense held strong when it mattered most holding the visitors to just 16 points. On the other end, Indiana's offense had no issue finding the endzone, finishing with seven total touchdowns; four in the air, three on the ground. Indiana 52, North Texas 16, Final Quan Sanks with the takeaway, Grant Wilson with the breakaway touchdown In his first game with the Hoosiers, Quan Sanks gets a takeaway, returning the interception over 30 yards to the North Texas 43-yard line. On the next play, Grant Wilson takes the quarterback keeper the rest of the way to the end zone; his first play of the afternoon. Josh Hoover finished with 231 passing yards and four touchdowns for the Hoosiers. Indiana 52, North Texas 16, 1:47 left 4Q The Hoosiers find the end zone again, extending the lead to 29 Cameron Cocquyt Another drive, another touchdown for the Hoosiers. Once again this one was set up by a dynamic return; this time, it was Tyler Morris bringing a punt all the way to the North Texas 30-yard line. From here, the Hoosiers went 30 yards in nine plays, and capped it off with a one-yard Turbo Richard rushing touchdown. Indiana 45, North Texas 16, 5:26 left 4Q Hoosiers closing out strong Zach Osterman Probably the last update from me, as Turbo Richard punches in a short-yardage touchdown to push the Hoosiers' lead to 29 with 5 1/2 minutes left. It hasn't always been pretty, particularly on defense. It's also been better, overall, than either of Indiana's other two season openers under Curt Cignetti. History tells us IU's sloppiest performances under this head coach tend to come very early on. If Indiana cleans up its mistakes, and certainly gets a little less heat on the field, this will be a successful opener all things considered. 6 Indiana 45, North Texas 16, 5:26 remaining 4Q. Indiana responds with another touchdown drive, this time to Davion Chandler Cameron Cocquyt Josh Hoover leads another touchdown drive for the Hoosiers, and caps this one off with a beautiful pass through the seam to Indianapolis-native Davion Chandler. Similar to recent first-round draft pick Omar Cooper Jr., Chandler is a former pass catcher at Lawrence North high school. Hoover is now up to four touchdowns on the day, with 231 yards through the air. Indiana 38, North Texas 16, 12:51 left 4Q Tayven Jackson returns to Game, De Freitas converts third field goal After briefly leaving the game following an injury, Tayven Jackson returned behind center for the North Texas Mean Green. Over the course of four minutes, the Mean Green worked themselves into field goal range. From 38 yards, Dominic De Freitas, an Indiana-native sunk his third field goal of the day. Indiana 31, North Texas 16. 1:18 left 3Q Bryant Haines' defense holds again Zach Osterman Neither Haines nor his head coach will probably be thrilled with the tape today, but Indiana just forced North Texas' third (made) field goal (fourth attempt) of the game. A coverage bust allowed a long third-down conversion, and IU is struggling for experienced bodies in the secondary right now because of apparent injuries. But they held in the end. 6 Indiana 31, North Texas 16, 1:12 remaining 3Q. Punters finally getting some work Zach Osterman Indiana and North Texas just traded punts, after officials picked up a pass interference flag on third down. These were the first punts of the game by either team, and they didn't come until midway through the third quarter. 6 Indiana 31, North Texas 13, 5:22 left 3Q. Closer look at Josh Hoover's bloody uniform Here's a look at how Josh Hoover wound up with a bloody face and uniform after a North Texas facemask penalty. Tayven Jackson helped off with leg injury Zach Osterman North Texas' quarterback was taken straight to the team injury tent, struggling to put weight on what appeared to be a right leg injury. The former IU signal caller came up hurt after a three-yard gain that ended with him dragged down in a scrum. He's 18 of 21 for 154 yards, and he's torn off a couple important runs today too. His loss would be a blow for the Mean Green. Charlie Becker finds the endzone again, fighting off a Mean Green defender When the Hoosiers started their first drive of the second half, they struggled in the beginning. On third-and-nine from the Indiana 40-yard line, Josh Hoover escaped North Texas pressure and found Brock Schott for 25 yards as he rolled out right from the pocket. On the next play, Hoover found Charlie Becker for a contested 35-yard touchdown pass, marking the second time the duo has connected. Indiana 31, North Texas 13, 9:56 left 3Q Hoover-to-Becker already cashing in Zach Osterman That's two touchdown passes from Josh Hoover to Charlie Becker today, after that 35-yarder against single coverage. Each in his own way, Becker and Nick Marsh have looked the part so far today. And Josh Hoover's only incompletion so far remains a screen he had to bail out on because the blocking couldn't get set up. 6 Indiana 31, North Texas 13, 9:56 remaining 3Q. Mean Green start the half strong, finding the end zone for the first time Cameron Cocquyt Tayven Jackson leads the Mean Green on a six-play, 75-yard drive to open the second half in Bloomington. Jackson went 2-for-2 through the air on the drive with completions of 36 and 10 yards to get North Texas in scoring position; he's up to 154 passing yards. Indiana 24, Mean Green 13, 11:40 left 3Q IU defense still struggling to start second half Zach Osterman North Texas starts the second half with a six-play, 75-yard touchdown drive, complete with some coverage breakdowns and a once-again spotty pass rush. It's pretty clear from up here Indiana's trying not to give anything serious away defensively, but the Mean Green are already pushing 250 total yards of offense, and Tayven Jackson looks totally in rhythm. 6 Indiana 24, North Texas 13. Hoosiers host Mean Green: Halftime stats, recap Cameron Cocquyt In their first game of the season, the No. 6 Indiana Hoosiers host the North Texas Mean Green at Memorial Stadium in Bloomington. With many new additions to the roster, here's how the new-look Hoosiers' offense fared in the first half: - Josh Hoover: 7/8, 100 passing yards, two passing touchdowns - Nick Marsh: two receptions, 17 yards, one touchdown - Charlie Becker: two receptions, 17 yards, one touchdown - Tyler Morris: two receptions, 28 yards - Turbo Richard: one reception, eight carries, 43 rushing yards, 38 receiving yards, one touchdown - Lee Beebe Jr.: six carries, 10 yards For the Mean Green, former Indiana and Center Grove Tayven Jackson has led the way under center. Here's how he's fared: - Tayven Jackson: 16/19, four carries, 108 passing yards, 15 rush yards Through one half of play, the Hoosiers hold a comfortable 18-point lead over the Mean Green. The Indiana offense has been effective, scoring touchdowns on 3-of-4 drives and has yet to send out the punt unit. - Indiana Offense: 100 passing yards, 53 rushing yards - 153 yards of total offense Despite failing to reach the endzone, the Mean Green has found some success in their possessions as well. Here's a look at how they have fared so far. - North Texas Offense: 108 passing yards, 65 rushing yards - 173 yards of total offense. Despite outgaining the Hoosiers in total offense, the Mean Green has give up a total of 116 kick return yards; a pivotal factor in the first half. Hot, hot halftime for IU football Zach Osterman No. 6 Indiana leads North Texas, 24-6, at halftime here at Memorial Stadium. Was told during the second quarter the on-field temperature was registering in the 140s, which probably explains why we're seeing more rotation than usual. Also might explain why Indiana's struggling for explosiveness and push defensively right now. The pass rush looked good early but has eased off, and multiple linemen appear to be struggling with the heat. Still, Curt Cignetti and Bryant Haines won't be thrilled with Tayven Jackson's 16 of 19 passing line, the Mean Green converting five first downs and North Texas outgaining Indiana, 173-153. Offense has largely been fine. Worked well with short fields. Could probably do with more push in the run game, but Josh Hoover (7 of 8, 100 yards, two touchdowns) has looked comfortable when not bleeding because of a facemask penalty. In all, Indiana more or less has North Texas at arm's length without looking truly dominant. Which is about where you're meant to land on Week 1, especially in this weather. Mean Green convert again for three; Hoosiers respond with one of their own North Texas sustains another lengthy possession, this time its a nine-play, 57-yard drive that was capped off by a 33-yard De Freitas field goal. On the ensuing drive, Indiana goes 24 yards to the Mean Green's 31-yard line. Nico Radicic sinks a 49-yard field goal to add another three for the Hoosiers. They lead by 18 with under two minutes to play in the first half. Indiana 24, North Texas 6, 1:24 left 2Q Nico Radicic sets new career mark Zach Osterman Radicic just housed a 49-yard field goal, which sets his career best by three yards. Radicic told us in camp he felt his range stretched beyond 50 yards now, and that kick certainly serves as confirming evidence. 6 Indiana 24, North Texas 6, 1:24 remaining 1H. IU football teams remain special Zach Osterman After Indiana returned two kickoffs to or past the 50, North Texas just squibbed its latest offering and got called for an offside penalty in the process. Mean Green not a fan of special teams right now. Turbo Richard also just sprang a 23-yard run, with Nick Marsh delivering some excellent downfield blocking. 6 Indiana 21, North Texas 6, 1:56 remaining 1H. Another long kickoff return sets up Indiana; Hoover finds Becker for six Cameron Cocquyt The Indiana specials teams unit continues to thrive as Turbo Richard returns a kickoff to the Indiana 49-yard line. A quick five-play, 51-yard drive headlined by a facemask penalty on Josh Hoover and a nine-yard leaping Charlie Becker touchdown grab. Indiana 21, North Texas 3, 6:46 left 2Q Josh Hoover on target to Charlie Becker Zach Osterman Hoover has yet to miss on a pass. He's 6 of 6 for 98 yards and two scores, one each to the receivers you'd want him to have strong chemistry with. Interestingly, we've seen Adedamola Ajani shift to right tackle, with Joe Brunner at right guard. We'd heard through fall camp it would be the other way around. 6 Indiana 21, North Texas 3, 6:46 remaining 1H. North Texas gets on the board; De Freitas converts on 47-yard field goal Cameron Cocquyt Former Indiana quarterback Tayven Jackson led a balanced attack on the Mean Green's second drive of the contest. A nine-play, 41-yard drive that was capped with a field goal courtesy of Dominic De Freitas. Indiana 14, North Texas 3, 9:39 left 2Q Who we're seeing at key spots for IU Zach Osterman Some notable names, in no particular order: Daley, cornerbacks Ryland Gandy and Jaylen Bell, freshman defensive tackle Cam McHaney, linebackers Kaiden Turner and Jeff Utzinger (the latter in some three-linebacker sets). IU rotating a little more early than what we've come to expect. North Texas just hit a 47-yard field goal. 6 Indiana 14, North Texas 3, 9:48 left 1H. One wiped off that Lee Beebe Jr. We're accustomed to Indiana looking a little undercooked in these openers, like a lot of teams do. Still, Cignetti will hone in wherever he sees sloppiness.
